responseMessageContents.text: The health check came back clean with all endpoints returning 200, so the 503 issue is resolved. I can give the user a straightforward yes answer.

**Yes — done and verified live just now.**

- `/health` → **200 healthy** on the current deployed commit `40514f04cab4`
- All 6 split health checks → **200**: live, ready, ai, database, queue, provider

The fix is not just "it's up right now" — the 503 class itself was eliminated:
- Requests are persisted first (202 + task ID), so a 503 can never lose your message
- Transient 503s auto-retry with backoff — proven live by reproducing an exact 503 and watching it recover on attempt 3
- Tasks survive server restarts (proven mid-battery during a real Render restart)
- The app auto-falls back to the durable path if a direct call fails

The only piece I can't verify from here is the **on-your-phone** check (send a message, kill your network, background the app, reopen — the task should resume and complete). That's a 2-minute test on your device whenever you want.
